target.title: fix(codex): project absolute thread tokenUsage into attemptUsage
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex-runtime users would see `/status` context oscillate between `?/N` and a real number after ordinary turns. OpenClaw projected only the per-call `thread/tokenUsage/updated.last` snapshot into attempt usage, so the absolute cumulative thread total from Codex app-server never reached session persistence as a fresh total.

Closes #107324

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex app-server streams absolute cumulative usage on `tokenUsage.total` and per-call usage on `tokenUsage.last`. Session context freshness needs the absolute thread total at the Codex adapter boundary so the existing generic session store can mark `totalTokensFresh` without weakening provider-neutral fallbacks. This PR prefers `total` when present and falls back to `last` only when the absolute snapshot is absent.

**Fix quality:** compatibility — additive projection change only at the Codex plugin boundary, no session-store / CLI semantics change; performance — one extra object-field read on an existing notification path; usability — restores stable `/status` context numbers after ordinary Codex turns; security — no auth, secret, or trust-boundary change.

Open alternate PRs that only preserve a stale `entry.totalTokens` with `totalTokensFresh: false` leave `/status` rendering `?` and do not match this boundary.

## User Impact

After ordinary Codex turns, `/status` context should keep a trustworthy used-token number instead of flipping to `?` until the next compaction.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (path-scoped closeout; full `pnpm check:changed` expanded into `pnpm install` and was stopped; quality floor covered by focused tests + format/diff checks).

```text
$ git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# PASS

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
# All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts \
    -t "projects assistant deltas and usage|projects absolute cumulative|falls back to per-call"
 ✓ |extension-codex| event-projector.test.ts (3 passed | 151 skipped)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Codex `thread/tokenUsage/updated` absolute cumulative `total` is projected into `attemptUsage` so session context can stay fresh after ordinary turns (issue #107324 / ClawSweeper acceptance).
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at branch `fix/107324-codex-absolute-thread-token-usage`, Node via repo Vitest wrapper.
- Current-main contrast: on main, `handleTokenUsage` only normalized `tokenUsage.last`. With both `total` and `last` present, `attemptUsage` reflected last-call fields (e.g. total=12) and ignored absolute cumulative total (e.g. totalTokens=900_000). Cumulative-only notifications left `attemptUsage` undefined.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts -t "projects assistant deltas and usage|projects absolute cumulative|falls back to per-call"`
  2. Cases exercise production `CodexAppServerEventProjector.handleNotification` + `buildResult` with realistic `thread/tokenUsage/updated` payloads.
- Evidence after fix: three focused tests passed in 72ms after import (see Evidence block). When both snapshots are present, `attemptUsage` is `{ input: 600000, output: 100000, cacheRead: 100000, total: 900000 }` (absolute total after uncached-input normalization). Cumulative-only notifications now project the absolute total. Last-only notifications still fall back correctly.
- Control check: last-only fallback test still asserts per-call last fields; sibling skipped tests in the same file were not modified except the renamed cumulative-only case. No session-store CLI branch changes.
- Observed result after fix: absolute Codex thread usage reaches `attemptUsage` / assistant usage so generic persistence can mark a positive fresh total instead of relying on compaction-only recovery.
- What was not tested: live managed Codex app-server end-to-end turn against a real account; full `pnpm check:changed` / `pnpm test:changed` (local pnpm expanded into install and was substituted with path-scoped static + focused Vitest).

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).
